podcast.body: This canon in B flat for six voices was written by Mozart in Vienna in 1782, likely as a party piece to elicit giggles from friends. Its lyrics were sanitized for nearly 200 years due to their gross nature, with the original versions only becoming widely public in 1991 after his widow attempted to have similar works published posthumously. "That's Kiss My Ass."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This work, despite being a beautifully structured and musically impeccable 6-voice canon, was an example of Mozart's irreverence. He used it to mock the nobility and challenge the seriousness of the world that applauded him, embodying his rebellious spirit. "Escribió obras como, perdón por la pronunciación, Legmissimarsh, que traducido significa, hum, un canon a 6 voces, vellamente estructurado y musicalmente impecable, que no paraba de repetir."

srcs.episode: El punk existía antes de Sex Pistols (y era algo salvaje)
